evidence: references pokedexNumber: Evolution.fromPokemon, Evolution.toPokemon, TeamSlot.pokemon, PokemonMove.pokemon, PokemonVariety.pokemon, Encounter.pokemon
findings.message: Relations to Pokemon reference different target fields. Mixing Pokemon.id and Pokemon.pokedexNumber is an ID-contract hazard for writes and joins.
findings.recommendation: Choose one stable target (prefer Pokemon.id surrogate key) and migrate all references with a verified mapping; keep pokedexNumber unique for public API identity.

findings.message: No Nature model. NatureDex is requested but no model exists.

evidence: models present: Pokemon, Type, Ability, Evolution, User, UserPokemon, Team, TeamSlot, Move, PokemonMove, PokemonVariety, Encounter, DexEntry, Item, Walkthrough
findings.message: No GameVersion model. Game-specific rules and walkthroughs use free-text version slugs.

evidence: models present: Pokemon, Type, Ability, Evolution, User, UserPokemon, Team, TeamSlot, Move, PokemonMove, PokemonVariety, Encounter, DexEntry, Item, Walkthrough
findings.message: No Region model. Regional dex membership is stored as string arrays.

evidence: models present: Pokemon, Type, Ability, Evolution, User, UserPokemon, Team, TeamSlot, Move, PokemonMove, PokemonVariety, Encounter, DexEntry, Item, Walkthrough
findings.message: No TypeEffectiveness model. Type chart is code-only; no per-generation rules can be stored or audited in DB.

evidence: PokemonMove fields: pokemonId, moveId, learnMethod, levelLearnedAt, pokemon, move
findings.message: Learnsets have no version/version-group dimension; the same move cannot be distinguished between games where it is or is not learnable.
findings.recommendation: Add versionGroup (and ideally learnMethod detail) with a stable FK.

evidence: Evolution fields: id, fromPokemonId, toPokemonId, fromPokemon, toPokemon
findings.message: Evolution stores only from/to IDs; triggers, levels, held items, friendship, time and version-specific conditions cannot be represented.

evidence: PokemonVariety fields: id, pokemonId, name, imageUrl, shinyImageUrl, isMega, isAlternative, types, pokemon
findings.message: Forms model has isMega/isAlternative but no Gigantamax flag or form-specific stats; form identity is incomplete.
Encounters reference locations and versions by free text instead of stable FKs.
Walkthrough gameVersion is free text; unsupported or misspelled slugs cannot be rejected by DB constraints.
Item has no relations to Pokemon, moves, encounters or game versions; item usage/availability cannot be modeled.
Seed uses a hardcoded species count as its sync range. Counts are not stable identifiers and become stale when new species are added.
findings.recommendation: Derive IDs from PokéAPI pagination/next URLs or a maintained explicit ID list.

findings.message: Update detection compares local row counts to API counts; gaps in IDs and renames cannot be detected and equal counts hide drift.

evidence: no special-case branch for generation <= 3 in damageCalc.ts
findings.message: Damage calculation uses move.damageClass unconditionally and has no Gen I special-stat or pre-Gen IV physical/special-by-type rules.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit per-generation battle rule adapters before claiming Gen I–IX support.

evidence: missing versions: ultra-sun, ultra-moon, sword, shield, scarlet, violet
findings.message: Curated walkthrough content does not cover every supported game version.

evidence: missing from admin options: red, blue, yellow, gold, silver, crystal, ruby, sapphire, emerald, firered, leafgreen, diamond, pearl, platinum, heartgold, soulsilver, black, white, black-2, white-2, x, y, omega-ruby, alpha-sapphire, sun, moon, ultra-sun, ultra-moon, lets-go-pikachu, lets-go-eevee, sword, shield, brilliant-diamond, shining-pearl, legends-arceus, scarlet, violet, legends-za
findings.message: CMS cannot create or edit walkthroughs for several supported games.
Nature data is hardcoded in the frontend and absent from Prisma/GraphQL; it cannot be audited, curated or versioned as data.
The server-side saveTeam mutation has no frontend caller; team builder state appears local-only, so DB team rows cannot be assumed complete.
Seed writes remote PokéAPI artwork URLs into DB image fields while local WebP assets are produced by the updater. Actual DB image URLs require runtime verification.
PokéAPI species IDs form a continuous range; the catalog contains no gaps.
Every frontend-supported game slug exists in PokéAPI and its generation agrees with the frontend mapping.
A game maps to a regional dex whose version groups exclude that game.
All mapped regional dex slugs exist in the PokéAPI pokedex catalog.
ID ranges used by the seed match PokéAPI species membership for all nine generations.
Audited species or variety names lack local normal/shiny WebP assets. DB imageUrl may still point to remote PokeAPI URLs; runtime verification is required.
Audited species do not expose both en and vi flavor text from PokéAPI; curated descriptions cannot be sourced from this reference alone.
Reference learnsets carry per-version-group detail, but the local PokemonMove model has no version dimension; imported learnsets cannot be validated per game.
